scenes.expected: The White Rabbit consults its waistcoat-pocket watch as Alice notices it. Pink eyes and white fur come from the source.
The same Rabbit hurries with white kid gloves and a large fan, splendidly dressed; the focal moment determines whether it is approaching or startled.
The White Rabbit mistakes Alice for Mary Ann and sends her for gloves and a fan. Preserve Alice as Alice, rather than introducing an actual second girl or fixing her earlier giant size.
Peter steps from the boat onto the water toward Jesus. Source context sets storm and time.
Peter recognizes the Lord and throws himself into the sea from the boat. Source context sets dawn and clothing.
The disciples find a charcoal fire with fish and bread ashore. Do not require Peter to appear when the selected source moment does not show him.

scope: Draft full Alice canon against the approved brief using the corrected identity partition; retain original source readings, moment boundaries and brief assignments.
Use existing runCanon, reference preparation and runSuite implementation with local stores; never write Convex or activate a generation.
Generate only Alice/White Rabbit stage sheets and the two needed style references. Other sheets remain absent and are reported.
Freeze each condition’s scene plans once; reuse candidate plans and reference identities for theme and model variations.
Retain failed attempts and normal check/retry outcomes. Never reroll a judged failure.
acceptance: Two independent scorers inspect every output and all sequence comparisons, with all disagreements retained or adjudicated.
Score source fidelity, recognizability, legitimate state changes, style adherence, artifacts and distinctive adaptation borrowing; absence or occlusion is unclear, not success.
Use same-scene repeat and cross-scene identity pairs; no forced person presence in the Bible control.
The baseline/candidate comparison changes canon and sheets together; it cannot attribute a gain solely to the reasoning setting.
A material source, identity or adaptation failure blocks promotion. Small samples and this limited Bible control cannot authorize public rollout; the existing release gates still apply.
